name: Static Color
notes:
Port of `static`, which is one `Background` of `color * brightness/255`. A `block` at `level` 1 covers the whole strip, which is what a Background is, and `over` is the blend a single opaque layer wants.

`color` IS THE ONE ANIMATION PARAMETER THE MACRO SURFACE CANNOT CARRY. It is a colour picker and a macro is a scalar, so the nearest knob is `palette.hueShift` -- and on this animation's default white that is a no-op, because hue rotates a hue and white has none. The knob starts working the moment the palette entry is given a colour. Nothing else in the fourteen has this problem: every other `color` sits on a shape whose default is already coloured, or on a palette.

`brightness` is `layer.opacity` rather than `palette.value`. Both would work here; opacity is the one that stays right when a second layer is added over this.
